description: Synthetic demo problems for the MongoDB demo database. Every person and figure is invented.

users.name: Aditya Kulkarni
users.bio: Backend developer working on internal tools.

users.name: Rahul Bansal
users.bio: Network engineer who teaches CCNA batches on weekends.

users.name: Priya Nambiar
users.bio: Visually impaired graduate student and screen reader user.

users.name: Karan Joshi
users.bio: Embedded developer building small IoT devices.

users.name: Sneha Reddy
users.bio: Product manager at a ten-person startup.

users.name: Zoya Mirza
users.bio: Web developer at a digital agency.

problems.title: Code reviews sit untouched for days in small teams
problems.description: Our team of five opens pull requests that wait three or four days for a review because nobody knows whose turn it is. Work piles up and merge conflicts get worse every day.

problems.title: Pull requests wait too long for someone to review them
problems.description: In our student project group, pull requests stay open for most of the week because reviewers are never assigned. By the time someone looks, the branch no longer merges cleanly.

problems.title: Code review comments are lost after a pull request is merged
problems.description: Useful design discussions happen in review comments, but once the pull request is merged nobody can find them again when the same question comes up months later.

problems.title: Local development setup takes new joiners two days
problems.description: Every new developer spends two days installing the right versions of Node, Python and the database, following an outdated wiki page. Small mistakes cause errors that take hours to find.

problems.title: New developers cannot get the project running on their laptops
problems.description: Interns joining our team struggle for days to run the project locally because the setup steps are scattered and half of them are out of date.

problems.title: Environment variables differ between every developer machine
problems.description: Each developer keeps their own .env file and nobody knows which settings are actually required, so bugs appear on one laptop and not on another.

problems.title: Flaky tests make the build fail at random
problems.description: About one build in five fails because of tests that depend on timing or network access. Developers rerun the pipeline until it passes and stop trusting the results.

problems.title: Nobody knows which API version the mobile app depends on
problems.description: Our backend changes response fields without warning and the mobile app breaks in production. There is no record of which app version needs which API version.

problems.title: Error logs are too noisy to find real problems
problems.description: The server writes thousands of warning lines an hour. When something genuinely breaks it is buried among messages nobody reads.

problems.title: Database migrations break when two developers add them at once
problems.description: Two branches each add a migration with the same number, and the second one fails after merging. We fix it by hand every sprint.

problems.title: Small projects have no simple way to track technical debt
problems.description: We keep saying we will clean up shortcuts later, but there is no list of what was skipped or how risky it is, so it is never prioritised.

problems.title: Release notes are written from memory the night before
problems.description: Nobody records changes as they happen, so release notes are incomplete and users are surprised by changes we forgot to mention.

problems.title: Dependency updates are ignored until something breaks
problems.description: Our projects use libraries that are two years out of date because updating feels risky. When a security fix arrives we cannot upgrade quickly.

problems.title: Code style arguments slow down every review
problems.description: Reviews turn into long debates about formatting and naming instead of logic, because the team never agreed on rules that a tool could check.

problems.title: Feature flags are left in the code for months
problems.description: Temporary switches for unfinished features stay in the code long after launch, and nobody remembers which ones are safe to remove.

problems.title: Junior developers do not know who owns which part of the codebase
problems.description: When something breaks in an unfamiliar module there is no list of owners, so questions go unanswered in the team chat.

problems.title: Estimating tasks is mostly guesswork
problems.description: Our sprint estimates are wrong by a factor of two because we never compare them with how long similar tasks actually took.

problems.title: Hotfixes skip the normal tests under pressure
problems.description: When production breaks, urgent fixes are pushed straight to the server without tests, and they often introduce new bugs.

problems.title: API documentation is always behind the code
problems.description: Our API reference is updated by hand and drifts from the real endpoints within weeks, confusing frontend developers.

problems.title: Merge conflicts in one shared configuration file
problems.description: Every feature touches the same large settings file, so almost every pull request ends in a merge conflict.

problems.title: Staging environment never matches production
problems.description: Bugs that only happen in production cannot be reproduced because staging uses different data and versions.

problems.title: Home Wi-Fi slows down badly every evening
problems.description: Between 8 and 11 pm our home broadband becomes almost unusable for video calls, even though the speed test in the morning is fine. The provider says nothing is wrong.

problems.title: Internet becomes very slow at night in our flat
problems.description: Every night our internet connection crawls and video calls freeze, but during the day everything works. We cannot tell whether it is the router or the provider.

problems.title: Neighbouring Wi-Fi networks interfere with ours in apartment blocks
problems.description: In our building dozens of networks overlap on the same channels, so signal strength looks good but speeds are poor. Nobody knows which channel to pick.

problems.title: College lab computers lose network access after every restart
problems.description: The computer lab has forty machines and several lose their IP address each morning. Students wait while the lab assistant reconfigures them one by one.

problems.title: Lab PCs show no internet until someone fixes the IP settings
problems.description: Half the machines in our department lab show limited connectivity every morning and need manual IP changes before practical sessions can start.

problems.title: Students cannot tell which lab machines are free
problems.description: During practicals students walk around the lab looking for a working, unoccupied computer because there is no shared status for the machines.

problems.title: Small offices have no idea which device is using all the bandwidth
problems.description: When the office internet slows down, there is no way for a non-technical owner to see that one computer is uploading backups all day.

problems.title: Students struggle to understand subnetting from slides
problems.description: Subnetting examples in lectures go too fast, and practising by hand gives no feedback on whether the network and broadcast addresses are correct.

problems.title: Guest Wi-Fi in clinics shares the same network as patient records
problems.description: Many small clinics give visitors the main Wi-Fi password, which puts patient computers and visitor phones on the same network.

problems.title: Rural schools lose connectivity whenever it rains
problems.description: Our village school uses a wireless link that drops during heavy rain, and online lessons stop for the rest of the day.

problems.title: Port forwarding instructions are confusing for home users
problems.description: People trying to host a game server or a camera viewer at home follow router guides that do not match their model and give up.

problems.title: Network cables in our office are not labelled
problems.description: When a desk loses connection nobody knows which switch port it uses, so tracing one cable can take an hour.

problems.title: DNS problems look like the whole internet is down
problems.description: When our provider's DNS server fails, websites stop loading but apps that use IP addresses still work. Staff report it as an outage and nobody knows the cause.

problems.title: Hostel Wi-Fi requires logging in again every hour
problems.description: The hostel captive portal logs everyone out every hour, interrupting downloads and video lectures.

problems.title: No easy way to check if a website is down for everyone or just me
problems.description: When a site does not load, students cannot tell whether the problem is the campus network, their device or the website itself.

problems.title: Video calls are choppy even on fast connections
problems.description: Our upload speed is fine on paper, but calls still stutter. We do not understand latency and jitter well enough to fix it.

problems.title: Router firmware is never updated in small businesses
problems.description: Most shop routers run years-old firmware because owners do not know updates exist or fear breaking the connection.

problems.title: IPv6 is disabled because nobody understands it
problems.description: Our campus network turns IPv6 off on every device because the admins are unsure how addressing works.

problems.title: Printers disappear from the office network
problems.description: Network printers change IP address after a power cut and every computer loses them.

problems.title: Students confuse TCP and UDP behaviour in labs
problems.description: In lab exercises students cannot see why UDP packets are lost silently while TCP retransmits.

problems.title: Mesh Wi-Fi nodes are placed in the wrong spots
problems.description: Families buy mesh systems but place nodes where the signal is already weak, so coverage barely improves.

problems.title: Students cannot practise programming without a laptop
problems.description: Many first-year students only have a phone. They fall behind in programming labs because they cannot practise at home.

problems.title: Learners with only a smartphone cannot practise coding
problems.description: Students in our coaching centre do not own computers, so they only write code during the two lab hours each week.

problems.title: Online code judges are hard to use on slow connections
problems.description: Practice websites for programming load heavy pages and time out on rural mobile data, so students give up halfway.

problems.title: Group assignment marks do not reflect individual effort
problems.description: In group projects one or two students do most of the work but everyone gets the same mark, and teachers cannot see who contributed what.

problems.title: Teachers cannot tell who actually did the work in group projects
problems.description: Our group submissions get one grade for everybody, even when some members never contributed a single file.

problems.title: Peer feedback in group projects is never collected
problems.description: Students have useful opinions about how their teammates worked, but there is no simple anonymous way to share them with the teacher.

problems.title: Lab manuals are printed with outdated instructions
problems.description: Our practical manuals refer to software versions that are no longer installed in the lab, so every session starts with confusion.

problems.title: Students forget concepts a week after the exam
problems.description: We cram for exams and forget most of the material soon after, because there is no regular revision of older topics.

problems.title: Hindi-medium students struggle with English technical terms
problems.description: Students who studied in Hindi-medium schools understand the concepts but lose marks because technical vocabulary is never explained.

problems.title: Teachers spend weekends checking handwritten quizzes
problems.description: Short weekly quizzes help learning, but checking them by hand takes teachers most of the weekend.

problems.title: No record of which practical experiments a student completed
problems.description: When lab files are lost, students have no proof of which experiments they performed during the semester.

problems.title: Visually impaired students receive notes as scanned images
problems.description: Lecture notes are shared as scanned PDFs that screen readers cannot read, so blind students depend on classmates.

problems.title: Students do not know which electives lead to which careers
problems.description: Elective choices are made from a list of course codes with no information about the skills or jobs they lead to.

problems.title: Attendance shortage is discovered too late to recover
problems.description: Students only learn their attendance is below the limit near the exam, when it is already too late to attend extra classes.

problems.title: Viva questions are the same every year but nobody shares them
problems.description: Practical exams repeat similar questions, yet juniors have no organised way to prepare from seniors' experiences.

problems.title: Online lectures have no way to ask questions later
problems.description: Recorded lectures are useful, but students cannot ask a question about a specific moment and get an answer.

problems.title: Exam timetables clash for students with backlogs
problems.description: Students repeating a subject find two exams scheduled at the same time and only learn this on the hall ticket.

problems.title: Library books cannot be reserved in advance
problems.description: Students walk to the library only to find the reference book issued, with no way to join a waiting list.

problems.title: First-generation students do not understand credit systems
problems.description: Students whose parents never attended college do not understand credits, grades and backlogs until it is too late.

problems.title: Practical marks are entered late and contain errors
problems.description: Internal practical marks are typed from paper weeks later, and mistakes are found only after results.

problems.title: Physiotherapy patients stop doing home exercises
problems.description: Patients are given printed exercise sheets but stop after a few days because they forget the steps and nobody checks on them.

problems.title: Patients forget their prescribed exercise routine at home
problems.description: After each clinic visit, patients go home with a list of exercises but rarely complete them, and recovery takes much longer.

problems.title: Physiotherapists cannot see patient progress between visits
problems.description: Clinicians only learn whether exercises helped at the next appointment, two weeks later, with no data in between.

problems.title: Hospital beds are allocated using phone calls
problems.description: Ward staff phone each other to find an empty bed for an emergency admission, and patients wait in the corridor while they call around.

problems.title: Emergency staff do not know which wards have free beds
problems.description: When a patient needs admission, emergency doctors spend a long time calling wards because bed availability is not visible anywhere.

problems.title: Discharge paperwork delays freeing up hospital beds
problems.description: Patients who are medically ready to go home wait half a day for discharge papers, keeping beds occupied.

problems.title: Diabetic patients cannot read their glucose log trends
problems.description: Patients write glucose readings in a notebook but cannot spot patterns, and doctors have little time to review the pages.

problems.title: Lab reports use terms patients do not understand
problems.description: Blood test reports list abbreviations and ranges that confuse patients, who then search online and panic.

problems.title: Vaccination dates for children are easy to miss
problems.description: Parents keep vaccination cards at home and often miss due dates because nobody reminds them.

problems.title: Ambulance drivers cannot find addresses in new colonies
problems.description: New housing areas have no proper street names on maps, and ambulances lose valuable minutes asking for directions.

problems.title: Mental health support is hard to find for students
problems.description: Students who feel overwhelmed do not know whom to contact on campus and are afraid of being judged.

problems.title: Pharmacies run out of insulin without warning
problems.description: Patients only discover their insulin is out of stock after travelling to the pharmacy.

problems.title: Hospital visiting hours are not published anywhere
problems.description: Relatives arrive at the wrong time and are turned away because visiting hours differ by ward and are never published.

problems.title: Old prescriptions are lost when patients change doctors
problems.description: Patients rarely keep earlier prescriptions, so new doctors repeat medicines that already failed.

problems.title: Health camp registrations are done on paper
problems.description: Free health camps register hundreds of people on paper forms, and follow-up calls are impossible because the forms are unreadable.

problems.title: Sign language interpreters are unavailable at clinics
problems.description: Deaf patients struggle to explain symptoms because clinics have no way to reach an interpreter quickly.

problems.title: Patients cannot book follow-up visits easily
problems.description: Clinics ask patients to call back for follow-ups, the line is always busy, and patients skip the visit.

problems.title: Blood bank stock is not visible to hospitals nearby
problems.description: Hospitals phone blood banks one by one to find a matching unit during emergencies.

problems.title: Elderly patients mix up similar-looking tablets
problems.description: Patients taking many white tablets confuse them and take the wrong dose.

problems.title: Too many tools for one small team's tasks
problems.description: Our team tracks work in a spreadsheet, a chat app and email at the same time. Tasks fall through the gaps between them.

problems.title: Tasks are split across chat, email and spreadsheets
problems.description: We never know where a task was agreed. Some are in the group chat, some in email threads and some in a shared sheet nobody updates.

problems.title: Meeting notes are never linked to the tasks they create
problems.description: We write meeting notes, but the action items in them never reach the task tracker, so they are forgotten.

problems.title: Context switching between projects wastes hours every day
problems.description: I work on three projects and lose time restarting each one because I cannot remember where I stopped.

problems.title: I keep forgetting where I left off when I switch projects
problems.description: Every time I move from one project to another I spend half an hour working out what I was doing.

problems.title: Notifications interrupt deep work all day
problems.description: Chat and email notifications arrive every few minutes, making it impossible to concentrate on difficult tasks.

problems.title: Shared documents have five versions with different names
problems.description: We email files around and end up with final, final2 and final-really, and nobody knows which is current.

problems.title: Freelancers chase unpaid invoices manually
problems.description: I send reminders for overdue invoices by hand and often forget, so payments arrive months late.

problems.title: Scheduling meetings across time zones takes many emails
problems.description: Our team spans India and Europe, and finding a common slot takes long email threads.

problems.title: Personal to-do lists grow until they are useless
problems.description: My to-do list has two hundred items and I cannot tell which ones matter today.

problems.title: Receipts for reimbursement get lost before submission
problems.description: Paper receipts fade or get lost in bags before the monthly reimbursement deadline.

problems.title: Small teams do not know how long tasks actually take
problems.description: We have no record of time spent on recurring tasks, so planning the week is pure guesswork.

problems.title: Recurring weekly reports are rebuilt from scratch
problems.description: Every Friday I copy the same numbers from three systems into a report by hand.

problems.title: Bookmarks are scattered across browsers and devices
problems.description: Useful links are saved on my phone, laptop and work computer, and I can never find the one I need.

problems.title: Password resets waste time for office staff
problems.description: Staff forget passwords for a dozen systems and wait for IT to reset them several times a month.

problems.title: Handover between shifts misses important details
problems.description: When one shift ends, important pending items are passed on verbally and often forgotten.

problems.title: Team calendars do not show who is on leave
problems.description: People book meetings with colleagues who are on leave because leave is tracked in a separate sheet.

problems.title: Email threads with twenty people get out of control
problems.description: Decisions are buried in long reply-all threads and nobody knows the final answer.

problems.title: Common answers to customer questions are retyped daily
problems.description: Support staff type the same replies every day because there is no shared library of answers.

problems.title: Online forms cannot be completed with a screen reader
problems.description: Many college and government forms use unlabelled fields and image buttons, so screen reader users cannot tell what to type.

problems.title: Screen readers announce form fields as blank
problems.description: When I fill in admission forms online my screen reader only says edit text, so I guess which field is the name and which is the date.

problems.title: CAPTCHA blocks blind users from signing up
problems.description: Image CAPTCHAs on sign-up pages cannot be solved by blind users, and audio alternatives are missing or unclear.

problems.title: Videos in online courses have no captions
problems.description: Deaf and hard-of-hearing students cannot follow recorded lectures because most videos have no captions or transcripts.

problems.title: Recorded lectures are useless for deaf students
problems.description: Our university uploads lecture recordings without subtitles, so deaf students rely on friends' notes.

problems.title: Live online classes have no sign language support
problems.description: Live sessions move too fast for deaf students to follow even with auto captions, and no interpreter is available.

problems.title: Colour-only charts confuse colour-blind users
problems.description: Dashboards that show status only with red and green are unreadable for people with colour blindness.

problems.title: Public buildings do not list wheelchair access information
problems.description: Wheelchair users cannot check in advance whether an office has a ramp, lift or accessible toilet.

problems.title: Small text in mobile apps cannot be enlarged
problems.description: Several banking apps ignore the phone's font size setting, so older users cannot read balances.

problems.title: Keyboard users get trapped inside website pop-ups
problems.description: Pop-ups on many websites cannot be closed without a mouse, trapping keyboard-only users.

problems.title: Dyslexic students struggle with dense lecture slides
problems.description: Slides packed with text in small fonts are very hard to read for students with dyslexia.

problems.title: Elderly people cannot use self-service kiosks
problems.description: Ticket and payment kiosks have tiny buttons and time out quickly, so older people need help from strangers.

problems.title: Audio announcements at stations are not shown as text
problems.description: Platform changes are only announced by loudspeaker, so deaf passengers miss their trains.

problems.title: Accessible PDF guidelines are unknown to most teachers
problems.description: Teachers want to share accessible documents but do not know how to add headings and alt text.

problems.title: Low-vision users cannot read QR code menus
problems.description: Restaurants now show menus only through QR codes that open tiny, unreadable pages.

problems.title: People with tremors mis-tap small mobile buttons
problems.description: Tiny, closely spaced buttons cause users with hand tremors to tap the wrong action repeatedly.

problems.title: Government portals time out before users finish reading
problems.description: Screen reader users need more time, but forms expire after a few minutes without warning.

problems.title: Online maps give no information about step-free routes
problems.description: Wheelchair users cannot plan routes that avoid stairs and broken pavements.

problems.title: Error messages are only shown in red text
problems.description: Form errors are indicated only by red colour, which some users cannot see.

problems.title: Small businesses reuse one password for everything
problems.description: Shop owners use the same simple password for email, banking and billing software, so one leak exposes everything.

problems.title: Our office uses the same password for every account
problems.description: Everyone in our small office knows one shared password that opens all our accounts, including the bank portal.

problems.title: Former employees still have access to company accounts
problems.description: When someone leaves, nobody removes their access to shared drives and social media accounts.

problems.title: Students fall for phishing emails about scholarships
problems.description: Fake scholarship emails ask students for bank details, and every term some students lose money.

problems.title: Fake scholarship messages trick students into sharing details
problems.description: Students receive convincing messages promising scholarships and enter their bank login on fake pages.

problems.title: Students cannot tell whether a website is genuine
problems.description: Many students do not know how to check a domain name or certificate before entering personal details.

problems.title: Clinic computers have no backups against ransomware
problems.description: A small clinic keeps all patient files on one desktop with no backup, so ransomware would wipe out years of records.

problems.title: Two-factor authentication confuses elderly users
problems.description: Older users get locked out when one-time codes expire before they find the message.

problems.title: Public Wi-Fi is used for banking without protection
problems.description: People log in to bank accounts on open café Wi-Fi without understanding the risks.

problems.title: Developers commit API keys to public repositories
problems.description: Student developers push code with secret keys in it, and the keys are abused within hours.

problems.title: Software on office computers is never patched
problems.description: Office PCs run years-old browsers and PDF readers because nobody is responsible for updates.

problems.title: SMS scams pretending to be electricity boards
problems.description: Messages threaten to cut power tonight unless a bill is paid through a link, and elderly people panic and pay.

problems.title: College portals do not log out on shared computers
problems.description: Students log in on library computers and the next person finds their account still open.

problems.title: No one knows what to do after a data breach
problems.description: When an account is hacked, small organisations have no checklist for what to change and whom to inform.

problems.title: Spoofed caller IDs make scam calls look official
problems.description: Scam callers appear to be calling from a bank's number, so people trust them.

problems.title: Children install apps with excessive permissions
problems.description: Kids install games that request access to contacts, location and microphone without parents noticing.

problems.title: Shared office computers have no individual logins
problems.description: Everyone uses the same Windows account on the office computer, so files and browser passwords are shared with all staff.

problems.title: USB drives spread malware between lab computers
problems.description: Students carry assignments on pen drives that infect lab machines again and again.

problems.title: Website login pages are served without HTTPS
problems.description: Several small business websites still accept passwords over plain HTTP.

problems.title: Apps stop working completely when the network is weak
problems.description: Many delivery and ticket apps show a blank screen on weak mobile data instead of saving work and retrying.

problems.title: Mobile apps freeze when the signal drops
problems.description: When I travel by train the apps I use just spin forever and lose what I typed when the signal weakens.

problems.title: Large app updates use up limited mobile data
problems.description: Apps push huge updates over mobile data, using a large part of a small monthly data pack.

problems.title: Old phones cannot install the apps people need
problems.description: Banking and government apps require newer Android versions, leaving people with old phones unable to use services.

problems.title: Required apps do not support older Android phones
problems.description: My parents' phone runs an older Android version and cannot install the apps their bank and pension office require.

problems.title: Apps drain the battery on budget phones
problems.description: Background syncing in popular apps empties cheap phone batteries by afternoon.

problems.title: Mobile app sign-up asks for too many permissions
problems.description: A simple calculator app asks for contacts and location, so users refuse to install it.

problems.title: Regional language support in apps is poor
problems.description: Many apps offer only English or partial translations that mix languages awkwardly.

problems.title: Push notifications are mostly advertisements
problems.description: Users disable all notifications because most are promotions, and then miss important alerts.

problems.title: Small shops cannot afford to build their own app
problems.description: Local shops want customers to order from a phone, but building and maintaining an app is too expensive.

problems.title: Mobile forms do not show the right keyboard
problems.description: Phone number fields open the full keyboard and email fields do not show the at sign, slowing everyone down.

problems.title: App storage fills phones with cached files
problems.description: Messaging apps fill phones with old media, and users do not know how to clean it up safely.

problems.title: Users cannot find where an app stores their data
problems.description: People want to export their own data from an app but there is no visible option.

problems.title: Testing apps on many Android devices is expensive
problems.description: Student developers cannot afford many phones to test layouts on different screen sizes.

problems.title: Dark mode in apps is inconsistent
problems.description: Some screens in an app stay bright white in dark mode, which is uncomfortable at night.

problems.title: App onboarding screens cannot be skipped
problems.description: Long introduction screens force users to swipe through five pages before they can do anything.

problems.title: Mobile apps ask for an account before showing anything
problems.description: Users want to browse first, but apps force sign-up on the first screen and many uninstall them.

problems.title: Apps cannot be used with one hand on large phones
problems.description: Important buttons are placed at the top of tall screens, out of reach for one-handed use.

problems.title: Offline maps in apps are out of date
problems.description: Downloaded maps in travel apps still show roads that were closed months ago.

problems.title: College website is impossible to use on a phone
problems.description: Our college website only works properly on a desktop. On phones the menus overlap and results pages cannot be zoomed.

problems.title: Our institute's website breaks on mobile screens
problems.description: Students try to check notices on their phones, but the website layout is broken and text runs off the screen.

problems.title: Important notices are buried in PDF links
problems.description: Websites publish every notice as a PDF with a file name instead of a title, so finding the right one takes ages.

problems.title: Small business websites load very slowly
problems.description: Local business websites built with heavy templates take ten seconds to load on mobile data, and customers leave.

problems.title: Our shop's website takes forever to open
problems.description: Customers tell us our website is slow on their phones. It has large images and many plugins we do not understand.

problems.title: Business owners cannot update their own website content
problems.description: Every small text change on a business website requires paying the original developer.

problems.title: Online payment pages time out during busy hours
problems.description: Fee payment portals crash on the last day, and students are charged fines for failing to pay on time.

problems.title: Search on content websites returns irrelevant results
problems.description: Site search finds pages only by exact words, so a search for fee refund misses the page titled refund of fees.

problems.title: Users are logged out while filling long web forms
problems.description: Session timeouts erase half-completed forms without warning.

problems.title: Websites ask for cookies consent on every visit
problems.description: Cookie banners reappear on every page, covering content on small screens.

problems.title: Event registration pages allow duplicate sign-ups
problems.description: People submit registration forms twice when the page is slow, and organisers clean duplicates by hand.

problems.title: Broken links remain on websites for years
problems.description: University pages link to documents that no longer exist, and nobody notices.

problems.title: Web dashboards show numbers without explanation
problems.description: Admin dashboards display counts and percentages without saying what they measure or over which period.

problems.title: Image uploads fail without a useful error
problems.description: Upload forms reject photos for being too large but only say something went wrong.

problems.title: Websites do not work when JavaScript fails to load
problems.description: On slow connections scripts fail to load and pages show nothing at all instead of basic content.

problems.title: Online exam portals crash under load
problems.description: When thousands of students log in for an online test at the same time, the portal stops responding.

problems.title: Web forms lose data when the back button is pressed
problems.description: Pressing back on a multi-page form clears every field already filled.

problems.title: Admin panels have no audit trail of changes
problems.description: When a record is changed in our admin panel, nobody can tell who changed it or when.

problems.title: Search results pages cannot be shared as links
problems.description: Filtered search results are lost when the link is copied, because filters are not stored in the URL.

problems.title: Water tank overflows because nobody switches the motor off
problems.description: Our building's water motor is switched on manually, and the overhead tank overflows almost daily because someone forgets it.

problems.title: Overhead water tanks keep overflowing in our society
problems.description: Every morning water runs down the walls because the pump keeps running after the tank is full.

problems.title: No way to know how much water is left in the tank
problems.description: Residents only find the tank empty when taps run dry, often late at night.

problems.title: Greenhouse temperature is checked only twice a day
problems.description: Our small greenhouse loses plants on hot afternoons because temperature and humidity are only checked by hand in the morning and evening.

problems.title: Farmers cannot monitor polyhouse conditions remotely
problems.description: Polyhouse owners have to visit the site to check heat and humidity, and crops suffer when conditions change in between.

problems.title: Drip irrigation runs on a fixed timer regardless of soil moisture
problems.description: Our irrigation timer waters the field even after rain, wasting water and harming roots.

problems.title: Classroom fans and lights stay on in empty rooms
problems.description: Electricity is wasted every evening because classrooms are left with lights and fans running.

problems.title: Lab equipment issue records are kept on paper
problems.description: Students borrow multimeters and Arduino kits, and the paper register makes it impossible to trace missing items.

problems.title: Home appliances fail without any early warning
problems.description: Fridges and pumps break down suddenly, although rising power usage could have shown a problem earlier.

problems.title: Cold storage temperature breaches go unnoticed at night
problems.description: Medicine and vaccine fridges warm up overnight after power cuts, and staff only discover it in the morning.

problems.title: Smart devices stop working when the internet is down
problems.description: Our smart plugs need a cloud server, so even basic switching fails during internet outages.

problems.title: Arduino projects are hard to debug for beginners
problems.description: Students cannot tell whether a problem is in the wiring or the code, and serial output gives little help.

problems.title: Parking lots have no count of free spaces
problems.description: Drivers circle the hospital parking lot looking for a space because there is no display of free spots.

problems.title: Old desktop computers end up in landfill
problems.description: Schools throw away old computers that could be refurbished for students who need them.

problems.title: Gas leaks in kitchens are detected too late
problems.description: Small eateries have no gas detectors, and leaks are noticed only by smell.

problems.title: Power cuts damage equipment when supply returns
problems.description: Voltage spikes after power cuts burn out routers and computers in small offices.

problems.title: Solar panels lose output because of dust
problems.description: Rooftop solar output drops for weeks before anyone cleans the panels, because nobody tracks generation.

problems.title: Hostel water heaters stay on all day
problems.description: Geysers in hostels run continuously and waste electricity because there is no timer or occupancy check.

problems.title: Sensor readings from IoT projects are lost when Wi-Fi drops
problems.description: Student IoT projects stop logging data whenever the Wi-Fi disconnects, leaving gaps in experiments.

community_reports.title: Nobody picks up my pull requests
community_reports.description: I open a PR, ping the group chat and still wait days. A simple rota for reviews would fix most of it.

community_reports.title: Evening internet is unusable for online classes
community_reports.description: My classes are at 9 pm and the connection keeps dropping exactly then. I need some proof to show the provider.

community_reports.title: I only have a phone and cannot do coding homework
community_reports.description: Our assignments need an IDE, but I only have an Android phone. I copy code into notes and test it the next day in the lab.

community_reports.title: My father skips his knee exercises
community_reports.description: The physiotherapist gave him a sheet, but he does not remember the order or the counts, so he stopped after a week.

community_reports.title: I lose track of what my manager asked in chat
community_reports.description: Requests come in as chat messages and scroll away. I need one place where they become actual tasks.

community_reports.title: I could not submit an exam form without help
community_reports.description: The exam registration page had no labels at all. I had to ask a friend to fill it in for me.

community_reports.title: We share one login for the billing software
community_reports.description: Five staff use the same billing login, so we cannot tell who changed an invoice.

community_reports.title: Lost my form when the network dropped
community_reports.description: I filled a long application on my phone and lost everything when the signal went for a second.

community_reports.title: Cannot read exam notices on my phone
community_reports.description: The notice board page shows tiny text and I have to zoom and scroll sideways for every line.

community_reports.title: Tank overflow wasted water again today
community_reports.description: Our society wastes hundreds of litres every week because nobody knows when the tank is full.

solutions.title: ReviewRota
solutions.description: Assigns pull request reviewers in rotation and posts a daily summary of waiting reviews to the team chat.

solutions.title: DevSetup Script
solutions.description: A single script that checks tool versions and sets up the local environment, with clear error messages.

solutions.title: NightSpeed Logger
solutions.description: Runs speed and latency tests every 15 minutes and produces a chart to share with the internet provider.

solutions.title: Subnet Trainer
solutions.description: Practice questions for subnetting with instant feedback on network, broadcast and host ranges.

solutions.title: PocketIDE Lite
solutions.description: A lightweight browser code runner that works on phones and caches exercises offline.

solutions.title: ExerciseBuddy
solutions.description: Shows each home exercise with a short video and counts repetitions, with weekly progress for the physiotherapist.

solutions.title: BedBoard
solutions.description: A live ward bed board that nurses update from their phones.

solutions.title: TaskInbox
solutions.description: Turns starred chat messages and emails into tasks in one list.

solutions.title: FormLint
solutions.description: A browser extension that highlights unlabelled form fields for web developers.

solutions.title: VaultLite
solutions.description: A simple shared password vault for small offices with per-person access.

solutions.title: OfflineForms
solutions.description: An Android library that saves form drafts locally and submits them when the network returns.

solutions.title: NoticeBoard
solutions.description: A mobile-first notice page with search and plain-text notices instead of PDF links.

solutions.title: TankGuard
solutions.description: An ESP32 float-switch controller that stops the pump when the tank is full and sends a phone alert.
